key_insight: Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 switches polarization through a dynamic cooperative exchange between 3-coordinated and 4-coordinated oxygen atoms, rather than by simple atomic displacement.
engineering_relevance: This suggests memory-device design should preserve cooperative oxygen-exchange pathways to improve endurance and scaling while avoiding reliance on large strain-driven switching.
method: Electric-field-induced molecular dynamics on a defect-free HZO lattice
Machine-learning force field (MACEField) fine-tuned for accurate transient switching dynamics
Trajectory analysis of oxygen coordination changes and local volume response
evidence_signal: The simulations dynamically reproduced the P–E hysteresis loop and revealed a transient detour path, cooperative O3c/O4c exchange, and internal self-compensation of local expansion and contraction.
watch_item: The result is based on an idealized defect-free lattice, so real-device defects, interfaces, and processing variability may alter the switching pathway.
paper_title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
